definitions.meaning: a songbird is a flier, a thing that flies
an infection of the mouth common in babies and small children

explanation.surface: Someone who files papers makes an infantile grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sense and the fungal infection that often affects infants' mouths share the one word; 'making' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a common songbird, which flies, and a yeast infection that babies often catch.

clue.text: Parts, yet maybe gets together — that's material

indicators.note: maybe means the letters of parts and yet might come together in another order

explanation.surface: Separate bits are brought together to make a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall hanging is a heavy decorative fabric.

indicators.note: on means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: the rest are the others
rain falls, so a fall of water

explanation.surface: Falling on others while in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check.
The word means both brawls and remnants or leftovers.

clue.text: The man seeking perfection wants ties laid out

indicators.note: laid out means the letters of ties and laid are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfectionist needs his neckties neatly laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns TIES + LAID into a new order; 'laid' is fodder as well as part of the surface phrase 'laid out'. 'wants' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pursues ideals is one who seeks perfection.

indicators.note: involving means the reversed word wraps around the a
in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A political assembly is involved in a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LID into DIL, which then holds A. The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish parliament's lower chamber is a legislative assembly.

clue.text: Account the clerk free from error

parts.note: a curate is a clerk in holy orders, a junior clergyman

explanation.surface: The bookkeeper's ledger is spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clerk' looks like an office worker but is the old church sense, a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and correct work contains no mistakes.

clue.text: Accustomed to being rude in dreadful fashion

indicators.note: in dreadful fashion means the letters of rude in are muddled up

explanation.surface: Used to someone behaving terribly badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double duty in the surface but is only fodder: RUDE IN rearranged. 'to being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hardened or habituated to something means being used to it.

clue.text: The heartless having the right to impose some restriction

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cruel people claiming the authority to place limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes H, the centre of THE, leaving TE. 'having' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie an animal by a rope limits how far it can roam, imposing a limit.

parts.note: spent means past, over and done

explanation.surface: Money is spent on buying something to eat on the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked dough is a kind of food.

definitions.meaning: to disregard or leave out of account
a cut in price offered to a buyer

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to disregard; as a noun it is a price cut given as a special offer.

clue.text: One may expect people to go to pot at this hour

definitions.text: One may expect people to go to pot at this hour

parts.words: One may expect people to go to pot at this hour
parts.note: go to pot suggests ruin, but here people gather round the pot of tea served in the afternoon

explanation.definitionFit: The afternoon hour for drinking from the pot of tea.

parts.note: the head of skin is its first letter, S
tripped, as in tripping the light fantastic, means danced

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth danced in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a youth with a shaved head, but it splits into 'skin' and its head, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped means with clothes removed, so bare or undressed.

clue.text: First woman to go to King George I in distress

indicators.note: to go to means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: GRI stands for Georgius Rex Imperator, King George as emperor
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Eve visits a distressed monarch, George the First.
explanation.walkthrough: GRI, Latin for George King Emperor, appeared on coins and postboxes. The definition is loose: to be in distress is to mourn.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn or sorrow is to be in distress over a loss.

indicators.note: displaying means the letters are on show inside militant rumanian

explanation.surface: A fiery Romanian leader shows a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans MiliTANT RUManian; Rumanian is the older spelling of Romanian.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of rage or bad temper.

clue.text: Rugby union not out for defeat

parts.note: a batsman who is not out is still in, in cricket

explanation.surface: A rugby union side, not yet dismissed, heads for a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin someone is to destroy or bring them down, a kind of defeat.

indicators.note: alternative means an alternative arrangement of the letters of the last

explanation.surface: Keeping things hidden is the final option left.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by stealth means acting covertly, in secret.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means fed is written bottom to top

parts.note: an ender is the one that ends, the last

explanation.surface: Bored with the most recent title-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' looks like boredom; 'up' turns FED into DEF. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion defends a title or a cause, so is its protector.

definitions.note: read as Flora is, a member of the flora

indicators.note: about means prose goes round rim

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing, not verse
a rim is a lip or edge

explanation.surface: Flora speaks plainly about someone's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name; it is plant life, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow spring flower is a member of the plant kingdom.

clue.text: A set grin affected by the most irritated

indicators.note: affected means the letters of a set grin are altered

explanation.surface: A fixed smile is put on by the crossest person.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of cross or annoyed.

clue.text: Sociable creature living in a high-rise building

definitions.text: Sociable creature living in a high-rise building

parts.words: Sociable creature living in a high-rise building
parts.note: seems to describe a flat-dweller in a tower block, but means a social insect in its tall earth mound

explanation.definitionFit: These insects live in colonies and build towering mounds of earth.

clue.text: Many were in a hurry to get a quantity of herrings

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Lots of people rushed to buy a catch of herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is an old Scottish measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of fresh-caught fish used in Scottish fisheries.

parts.note: less means without
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: The landlord has no gold.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lets property to a tenant.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
can't means cannot

explanation.surface: Soldiers say they cannot, and refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back or disavow a statement.
The word means both a melody or passage of music and a breed or ancestral line.

clue.text: The number of the Spanish flat

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
flat means level or even

explanation.surface: A request for the number of the Spanish apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it means level, EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a number, one more than ten.

indicators.note: contrary means the letters of some and curt are put the other way about, in a new order

explanation.surface: A rather brusque, awkward client.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop is a regular buyer there.

parts.note: O is zero, none
ran means managed

explanation.surface: Nobody managed to reach the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Oran is a port in Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour city on Algeria's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Flag to stop on a road

parts.note: to stand is to stop still

explanation.surface: A signal to halt traffic on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner or ensign carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Do better than an individual gangster

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo it
one means a single person

explanation.surface: Outdo a lone gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago mobster of the Prohibition era.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Withdrawing interest' (8): 'Withdrawing' defines the answer but 'interest' gives neither a second definition nor wordplay for it; part of the clue looks lost and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: Object when put in temper-ary accommodation

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: A protest at being housed in short-term lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest, but it is the noun meaning aim; 'when put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An intent is an aim or purpose, the object of an action.
